content.text:
I submitted index 9 (Sb fraction 0.45) as the best composition. It had the highest EQE, but that was only 0.00198%. Every composition I measured showed essentially no photoresponse, so this is the least-bad point, not a good photoanode.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.22 | 0.00062 |
| 4 | 0.30 | 0.00093 |
| **9** | **0.45** | **0.00198** |
| 15 | 0.65 | −0.00064 |
| 22 | 0.80 | 0.00035 |

- **Why the signal is so low:** the two main zinc antimonate phases (Zn₇Sb₂O₁₂ spinel near 0.22 and ZnSb₂O₆ trirutile near 0.67) both have band gaps of about 3.3 eV or more. The 2.4 eV illumination is below that gap, so near-zero EQE is what you'd expect.
- **The ranking is shaky:** the differences are a few thousandths of a percent, which may be within measurement noise. Before the last two measurements, the model predicted about 0.0003–0.0006% with an uncertainty of about 0.0009% for the points it ranked highest. So index 9 beating the others is not strongly established.
- **XRD didn't help much:** I used three of the five XRD measurements, at indices 0, 9 and 18. The patterns are mostly the FTO substrate. Indices 9 and 18 add a weak film peak near Q≈2.44, and index 18 has a second one near Q≈3.62. I didn't match these to any database phase, so the idea that index 9 is a mixed-phase region is a guess.
- **Budget:** all five EQE measurements are used. Two XRD measurements were left over.

The remaining 23 compositions were never measured, including everything between 0.45 and 0.65 Sb.
